legacy_root.title: A3 package-boundary migration for five live trees without a wipe-and-reinstall
legacy_root.question: Design the packaging migration: which of today's live trees (two skills trees, hooks, rules, commands) become packages, where the package boundary falls, how already-deployed unpackaged content is ADOPTED in place rather than wiped and reinstalled, and what the uninstall contract must preserve (owner edits, user data, the curated MCP enable/disable state that must never be destroyed).

live_trees.boundary: one package per skill directory; source bytes are published, not uninstalled from live
SKILL.md is claimed in place; sibling owner-authored files stay unclaimed overlays
one package per hook json file
one package per rule markdown file
one package per command markdown file

package_boundary.unit: one lockfile-pinned package per capability id, not per tree
package_boundary.rule: A file is claimed iff it is the payload of a named capability (skill SKILL.md, hook json, rule md, command md, or a top-level runtime module on a real tools tree). Sibling owner files, user data, MCP enable/disable state, test suites, and publishable source copies are outside the boundary.
never_claim: owner-authored overlays beside a claimed capability

steps: Inventory the five live trees and classify each file as payload, overlay, user-data, MCP state, or source-only.
For each payload file, emit a package manifest that records path+sha256 of the bytes already on disk.
Do not rewrite claimed files; adopt means lockfile-pinning existing bytes.
List every file the package would NOT claim and the reason (owner edit, user data, MCP state, source tree, tests).
Refuse wipe-and-reinstall: uninstall later may delete only the claimed paths.
adoption_procedure.notes: C:/Users/Prekzursil live trees are absent on this Linux host. The five-tree estate is a disclosed fixture whose skill/hook/rule bytes come from the real ARC-0010 generator. Adoption is also demonstrated on the real tools/command-center tree.

uninstall_contract.removes: only files listed as claimed in the adopted package lockfile
forbids: resetting MCP enable/disable to package defaults

provenance_procedure.notes: Signal 1 is a Python sha256 of preserved files vs a snapshot. Signal 2 is bash cmp -s plus stat byte size. Timestamps never authorise deleting an unclaimed file.

signals.reads: byte identity of owner overlay, user-data, and MCP state after uninstall
cmp exit code and byte-size equality (different shell, different field)

decision_table.when: file is payload of a capability id
decision_table.do: CLAIM; record sha256; do not rewrite

decision_table.when: file is owner overlay / user-data / MCP state

decision_table.do: DO-NOT-CLAIM as installed; it is the package source

decision_table.when: wipe would remove a hand-authored file
sha256 intact count disagrees with bash cmp intact count
decision_table.do: BLOCKED with both numbers; do not pick a winner
